answers.falsifier: Done when: (1) --dry-run prints the resolved context state and claude command with the bash's flag semantics (--1m wins over a 200K environment, --200k imposes, env then file default 200K); (2) a held instance moves to the next free one; (3) the preflight runs floor.py verify then apply, and its residue rides --append-system-prompt, empty when the floor is up; (4) the ground loop and web server start through the launch tool, never when --dry-run, the web server not when port 80 listens or the box is not the cairn home; (5) the restart flags relaunch with --continue or fresh, DO_NOT_RESTART wins; (6) claude is spawned with inherited stdio in this console; (7) the module has none of os.name, sys.platform, platform.system, a bash literal, or a sudo password flag, and no sudo prompt where the launch tool says shell scripts do not run. answers.how: New cairn/devices/cc/superclaude.py porting the 882-line bash cairn/devices/cc/superclaude: flag parse and the context switch (command line > environment > file default), instance and held-instance move, session name and CAIRN_USER, preflight by calling recovery's floor.py as a subprocess CLI (RULE 1: cc may not import recovery) with the residue riding --append-system-prompt, memory_link.py, the CAIRN_FLOOR_FINDINGS carry-in, claude install when absent, the flags home and the restart loop (inner mode), the ground loop and web server via launch.service_spawn, port 80 via launch.port_listening, the trace wire, --dry-run, tmux mode, and the memory scope via launch.scoped_exec. Sudo is asked only where launch.runs_shell_scripts() is true. claude runs in THIS console with inherited stdio, as UnseenUniversity bin/superclaude.ps1 does. Every OS question goes through cairn/devices/system_rackmount/tools/launch/launch.py; the module has no os.name, sys.platform, platform.system test. The bash stays until bin/cairn.py dispatches to the .py (child 5).
answers.traces_to: Outline 10.3.2.1 and 5.4.3.8 (superclaude is Python; Windows needs no bash); RULE 1 (OS answers come from the system device's published tool; recovery is reached through its CLI); Law 1 (the settled launcher is ported, not re-derived); Law 3 (the proof measures the launch plan, not a claim).
